title: TrueNorth quest
description: One quest, `content/quests/<id>.json`. A quest is an ordered list of steps a character gives the player; finishing the last step completes it. Question scheduling belongs to the domain - a step names the pool, it does not pick from it.

levelId.description: The level this quest is played on. The level document lists the quest id too; validate-content is where the two are cross-checked.

giver.description: The character who offers the quest.

summary.description: One or two plain-language sentences shown in the quest log and announced in the live region when the quest is accepted.

questStep.title: Quest step document
questStep.description: One objective. `targetId` is deliberately an unbranded id: what it names depends on `kind` (a character for talk, a POI for visit or collect, a question pool for answer), and a union of brands is not a shape a schema can state.

prompt.description: What the player is being asked to do, in plain language, roughly CLB 4.

subject.description: Which bank an `answer` step draws from. Required on `answer` steps and forbidden elsewhere.

count.description: How many questions an `answer` step asks. The quest says how many; the FSRS scheduler says which, from the player's own review state. A quest that named the ids would make the scheduler decorative, and a scheduler that ignored the quest would make the step unbounded - so the quest owns the count and the pool, and the domain owns the choice.

questionPool.description: Optional narrowing of the draw to these ids, still ordered and filtered by the scheduler. Absent means the whole subject bank is eligible, which is the normal case; present is for a step that must stay on one topic.

dialogue.description: Lines spoken when the step starts. Present on `talk` steps; absent elsewhere. Subtitles are on by default, so this is the subtitle text as well as the dialogue text.

allOf.$comment: The draw specification belongs to `answer` steps and to nothing else, so a `talk` step cannot carry a stray subject or count that nothing reads. Only property names this object already declares appear here (ADR-0007).

fact.description: Whether this line states a fact about Canada and, if so, its source and verification. "Welcome to Parliament Hill" is flavour; "Ottawa is Canada's capital" is a claim, and a wrong claim in an NPC's mouth is exactly as wrong as one on a question card (ADR-0003).

expression.description: Named face pose on the speaker's rig, resolved by the same name in Rive and in the sprite atlas. Absent leaves the rig's default.
